Traces the trajectory from static word embeddings to contemporary LLMs for measuring culture. Argues that while newer models are more powerful, they aggregate across languages, communities, and periods — producing representations detached from identifiable social standpoints. Reviews how embeddings measured cultural associations, examines evidence that large generative models struggle to reproduce human population diversity, and discusses provisional solutions: steering methods and historically/socially bounded models.
